rounding.notes: Three decimal places as printed; dashes mean unavailable, not zero. No unrounded scores or dispersion are inferred.

notes: Published values transcribed without recomputation; unavailable fields are not inferred. Main experiment table row.

paper_variant.description: Documented paper benchmark, annotation-level evaluation with disjoint annotators/users, adaptation as stated in tables, and extended training as recorded; fingerprints unavailable.
paper_variant.mapping_evidence: Paper sections 3/6/7 and Table 5; all discrepancies are disclosed in provenance and the associated catalog spec. No equivalence to modern measured splits is asserted.

limitations: Paper rows are rounded reports, not measured run bundles. Run IDs, actual execution seeds, environments, checkpoint revisions, test fingerprints and standard deviations are unavailable.
The recovered commit postdates the paper. Code defaults are evidence for a proposed reproduction, not proof of each published execution configuration.
Reported paper variants never establish verified comparability with a new measured test fingerprint.
BREXIT Table 2 calls the positive class Offensiveness, but Appendix B, prompt examples and historical config use hate speech/hs. This record maps to hs with that conflict disclosed.
Paper describes instruction tuning but footnote names base Llama; historical CLI names Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Identifier mapping is documented, not a recovered checkpoint identity.
Section 6.2 says Named Adaptation-T in one sentence, while Tables 5/6 and historical LaMP require test/inference adaptation. This catalog maps IPA to test and preserves the inconsistency.
Decoder tables omit extended training flags; false is taken from matching historical filenames, not independently attested by the table. Text prompts can still use adaptation examples.
